add.text: The last surviving litoptern genera were Macrauchenia, Xenorhinotherium and Neolicaphrium.
Litopterns were divided into nine families, of which Proterotheriidae and Macraucheniidae were the most diverse and the last to survive.
Mount Pinatubo is an active stratovolcano in the Zambales Mountains on Luzon in the Philippines.
The oldest eruption of modern Pinatubo, Inararo, was also its largest.
The long axis of the Denham caldera runs parallel to the tectonic fabric of the Havre Trough, which lies west of the volcanic arc.
Historical eruptions at Raoul in the 19th and 20th centuries were small-to-moderate phreatic ones, and some formed ephemeral islands in Denham caldera.
Lake Chad once grew to at least ten times its present size as Lake Megachad, then the largest lake on Earth.
Some studies suggest the dry Bodélé basin supplies over half of the nutrient-rich dust that supports the Amazon rainforest.
Ksudach has had five known collapse events, which created its system of nested calderas.
Two lakes, Bolshoe and Kraternoe, lie within calderas at the summit of Ksudach.
The eastern lobe of the White River Ash is 2.5 centimetres thick 600 kilometres from Mount Churchill and extends to the Great Slave and Great Bear Lakes.
Archaeological data show some important trade routes were abandoned and new ones set up after the eastern White River Ash eruption, implying displaced people built new trade networks.
The last widely accepted aurochs cow from Jaktorów died of natural causes in 1627.
Subfossil finds suggest wild aurochs may have survived in northwestern Transylvania until the 14th to 16th century and in western Moldavia until probably the early 17th century.
The Azores–Gibraltar transform zone activated at about 30 Ma.
The zone appears as a ridge on the Atlantic Ocean floor and is still an earthquake zone today.
In 1887 Stejneger estimated that fewer than 1,500 Steller's sea cows remained when Steller found them, and argued extinction was already an immediate danger.

One study argues the sea cow was already a dead clade walking even without human influence, since natural climatic and sea level shifts had wiped out most of the population and the tiny remainder risked a genetic extinction vortex.
Tephra layers found with the 1831 sulphate peaks in ice chemically matched the most recent Plinian Zavaritski eruption, dated to the early 19th century.

The sulfur from the eruption is thought to have cooled the Northern Hemisphere by 0.5–1.0 °C, coincided with shifts in the Indian and African monsoons, and preceded famines including the Guntur famine of 1832 in India and the Tenpō famine in Japan.
Because Santa María had no recorded eruptions, local people did not recognise the earlier seismicity as a warning of an eruption.
New eruptions began in 1922 with a lava dome complex extruded in the crater left by the 1902 eruption.
Environmental laws passed to protect the declining passenger pigeon did little to improve its numbers.
The deforestation that endangered passenger pigeons was also worsened by the invasive chestnut blight, which greatly reduced American chestnut trees.
A 45 second black-and-white film of the Hobart Zoo's presumed last thylacine was shot in 1933 by naturalist David Fleay.
Since 1996 Australia has marked National Threatened Species Day on 7 September, the date the last known thylacine died in 1936.
The Sikhote-Alin meteoroid's mass before entering the atmosphere is estimated at about 90 tonnes.
Eyewitnesses saw a bolide brighter than the sun come out of the north and descend at about 41 degrees.
It was the largest earthquake to hit Chile since the magnitude 9.5 1960 Valdivia earthquake and the strongest worldwide since the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake.
The earthquake triggered a tsunami with waves up to 24.1 m that devastated several coastal towns in south-central Chile, with the worst damage at Constitución.
Kamchatka lies on the Okhotsk plate, and the Pacific plate subducts beneath it.
Through the Miocene the climate slowly cooled towards a series of ice ages.
Topographic changes in Africa weakened the Somali Jet while South Asian Summer Monsoon rainfall increased.
Most modern lineages of diatoms had appeared by the Late Miocene.
Kelp forests are formed by brown macroalgae and provide a unique habitat for marine organisms.
A wide range of sea life, including fish, uses kelp forests for protection or food.
Especially productive kelp forests tend to occur where oceanographic upwelling delivers cool, nutrient-rich water from depth to the surface layer.

Meridiolestidans are generally classified within Cladotheria, closer to living marsupials and placental mammals than to monotremes, though one study recovered them as sister to spalacotheriid "symmetrodonts".
A possible meridiolestidan is known from a tooth fragment, now lost, from the Eocene La Meseta Formation of the Antarctic Peninsula.
Ground sloths evolved early, in the late Paleogene and Neogene, while South America was isolated.
Ground sloths ranged from under 100 kilograms in the Caribbean forms to 3,700–4,100 kilograms in the largest genera Megatherium, Lestodon and Eremotherium.
The expansion of grasslands in North America led to an explosive radiation among snakes.
Notoungulates and other South American native ungulates reached their peak diversity in the Eocene and Oligocene.
The group's diversity declined during the Pliocene and Pleistocene, at the same time as the Great American Interchange let North American ungulates and other mammals enter South America.
The Valencia Trough opened between the Late Oligocene and early Miocene, at the same time as the Provençal Basin.
Global temperatures stayed fairly steady through the Oligocene and early Miocene, and Antarctic glaciation waned during that time.
About 15 million years ago the Southern Hemisphere ice cap began to grow to its present form, as oceans cooled partly from the Antarctic Circumpolar Current.
Submerged masses like Zealandia, which includes present-day New Zealand, would be considered a continent.
The Indo-Australian plate is still driven under the Tibetan Plateau, pushing it up at about 5 mm per year, though erosion reduces the actual gain in height.
The Tibetan Plateau is the world's largest and highest plateau above sea level, with an area of 2,500,000 square kilometres.
Gymnosperms, including seed ferns, conifers, cycads and ginkgos, could reproduce by seeds from the Devonian.
The African Great Lakes region holds the source of the Nile and several large lakes of the Nile system, including Lake Victoria, Lake Albert, Lake George and Lake Edward.
The East African Rift is an intracontinental rift basin with active volcanism.
